description: A `{ return 1 }` arm of a DECL-position multi-scrutinee `match` (`const v = match (a, b) { … }`) returns 1 from the function — it does not become `v`. `pick(.A, .A)` is 1 (not 10); `pick(.B, .A)` is 30.
rationale: §19.3.3: "`fail` SHALL be valid inside any control flow construct (if/else, for, match) within a `!` function body. The `fail` returns from the function, not from the control flow construct." §19.4.3 (S451 ruling 1a) counts an arm that ends in `return` / `fail` — or a `break` / `continue` to a loop enclosing the statement — as LEAVING. impl#1 lowered a statement-position `match` to an IIFE, so these exits left only the arm: the statements after the `match` ran, a `fail` was dropped, and a `continue` was a JS syntax error (g-stmt-match-block-return-falls-through; dpa-068 D2/D3). The statement-position match now lowers inline. The decl-position multi-scrutinee match was still the value IIFE, where `return 1` made `v = 1` and the function went on to return 10.
